titular: Nvidia bets on crypto platforms plunge 7% overnight
resum: Contracts that track Nvidia's shares on the crypto platform Hyperliquid fell 7% after news that the board could oust Jensen Huang, while bitcoin barely moved. These contracts trade 24 hours a day, including when the stock market is closed.
per_que_importa: These products, called "perpetuals", let people bet with borrowed money (leverage): a small drop can wipe out everything put in. And they lack the protections of a regulated brokerage account.

titular: Customers pull $126m from MEXC after the US cuts it off from the financial system
resum: The US Treasury accuses the MEXC platform of moving more than $16bn linked to cybercrime and sanctions evasion, and bars US banks from making transfers to it. About $126m in net outflows followed in the next 24 hours; MEXC says it is operating normally.
per_que_importa: When a platform comes under suspicion, customers can find their money frozen or held up by checks. Unlike a bank, there is no deposit guarantee scheme covering the funds.

titular: Stablecoins shrink at the fastest pace since 2022
resum: The total supply of stablecoins (cryptocurrencies pegged to the dollar) fell by $14.2bn in the 30 days to 9 November, the fastest contraction since June 2022, according to Glassnode. Just under $280bn is now in circulation, while bitcoin funds keep losing money.
per_que_importa: Stablecoins are the "cash" investors use to move around the crypto world: if they're withdrawn, appetite for risk is falling. It's also a reminder that, despite the name, they depend on the solvency of the company that issues them.

titular: Few European crypto firms are licensed to operate in Spain
resum: According to a count by CriptoNoticias, only 16 in every 1,000 European crypto firms are authorised to offer services in Spain, including Spanish platforms such as Bit2Me and Criptan. Since July, only firms authorised by Spain's market regulator (CNMV) or another European supervisor under the EU's MiCA rules may operate.
per_que_importa: Using an authorised platform doesn't guarantee making money, but it does mean there's a supervisor to complain to and minimum rules. Before opening an account, you can check the CNMV register to see whether the firm is listed.

titular: A Robinhood Chain platform loses $2.23m to an accounting bug
resum: Arcus, a crypto contracts platform on Robinhood's network, has lost about $2.23m: a new account exploited a bug in transfers between sub-accounts to receive a balance it never had and withdraw it. The company says it will absorb the loss.
per_que_importa: Coding errors on these platforms can drain funds in minutes. This time the company is covering it, but that isn't always the case: in crypto there is no public fund that gives money back.
